arxiv-2110-00358.title: Non-minimal geometry-matter couplings in Weyl-Cartan space-times: f ⁡ ( R , T , Q , T m ) f(R,T,Q,T_{m}) gravity
arxiv-2110-00358.creator: Tiberiu Harko, Nurgissa Myrzakulov, Ratbay Myrzakulov, Shahab Shahidi
arxiv-2110-00358.description: Abstract We consider an extension of standard General Relativity in which the Hilbert-Einstein action is replaced by an arbitrary function of the Ricci scalar, nonmetricity, torsion, and the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. By construction, the action involves a non-minimal coupling between matter and geometry.

arxiv-2112-04374.title: Dependability Engineering in Isabelle
arxiv-2112-04374.creator: Florian Kammüller
arxiv-2112-04374.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a process of formal system development supported by interactive theorem proving in a dedicated Isabelle framework. This Isabelle Infrastructure framework implements specification and verification in a cyclic process supported by attack tree analysis closely inter-connected with formal refinement of the specification.

arxiv-2205-07112.description: Abstract Forward-secure signatures guarantee that the signatures generated before the compromise of private key remain secure, and therefore offer an enhanced compromise-resiliency for real-life applications such as digital forensics, audit logs, and financial systems. arxiv-2311-04186.title: Resource analysis of quantum algorithms for coarse-grained protein folding models
arxiv-2311-04186.creator: Hanna Linn, Isak Brundin, Laura García-Álvarez, Göran Johansson
arxiv-2311-04186.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hanna Linn, Isak Brundin, Laura García-Álvarez, Göran Johansson. Protein folding processes are a vital aspect of molecular biology that is hard to simulate with conventional computers. Quantum algorithms have been proven superior for certain problems and may help tackle this complex life science challenge. We analyze the resource requirements for simulating protein folding on a quantum computer, assessing this problem’s feasibility in the current and near-future technological landscape.

arxiv-2312-00606.creator: Helge Holden, Nils Henrik Risebro
arxiv-2312-00606.description: Abstract . We study a generalized Follow-the-Leader model where the driver considers the position of an arbitrary but finite number of vehicles ahead, as well as the position of the vehicle directly behind the driver. It is proved that this model converges to the classical Lighthill–Whitham–Richards model for traffic flow when traffic becomes dense.

arxiv-2502-05532.title: Nonlocal Micromagnetics: Compactness Criteria, Existence of Minimizers, and Brown’s Fundamental Theorem
arxiv-2502-05532.creator: Giovanni Di Fratta, Rossella Giorgio, Luca Lombardini
arxiv-2502-05532.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the existence and qualitative properties of minimizers for a class of nonlocal micromagnetic energy functionals defined on bounded domains. The considered energy functional consists of a symmetric exchange interaction, which penalizes spatial variations in magnetization, and a magnetostatic self-energy term that accounts for long-range dipolar interactions.

pmc-10570723.title: Adaption and validation of simplified Chinese version of the Low Back Pain Knowledge questionnaire (sC-LKQ)
pmc-10570723.creator: Zhe Wang, Yinyao Xie, Olívia Dózsa-Juhász, Alexandra Makai, Melinda Járomi
pmc-10570723.description: IntroductionLow back pain (LBP) knowledge questionnaire (LKQ) was developed by a Brazilian research group in 2009. It has been cross-culturally adapted to many languages with good reliability and validity. This work aimed to translate and validate the LKQ into a simplified Chinese version and to evaluate the self-efficacy in LBP among Chinese participants from China and Hungary.

pmc-10647647.title: Simplified Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Channel Prediction in Power Domain NOMA System
pmc-10647647.creator: Mohamed Gaballa, Maysam Abbod
pmc-10647647.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this work, the impact of implementing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) in predicting the channel parameters for user devices in a Power Domain Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access system (PD-NOMA) is investigated. In the channel prediction process, DRL based on deep Q networks (DQN) algorithm will be developed and incorporated into the NOMA system so that this developed DQN model can be employed to estimate the channel coefficients for each user device in NOMA system.

pmc-11321007.title: Patient responsiveness as a safewards fidelity indicator: a qualitative interview study on an acute psychiatric in-patient ward
pmc-11321007.creator: Veikko Pelto-Piri, Lars Kjellin, Gabriella Backman, Karoline Carlsson, Anna Björkdahl
pmc-11321007.description: BackgroundThe Safewards model aims to reduce conflict and use of containment on psychiatric wards. To evaluate the implementation of Safewards and understand why it is effective in some settings but not in others, it is important to assess the level of implementation fidelity.

pmc-11504185.title: Alien Rainbow Trout Oncorhynchus mykiss in the Balkhash Basin (Kazakhstan, Central Asia): 50 Years of Naturalization
pmc-11504185.creator: Nadir Shamilevich Mamilov, Marlen Tursynali, Gulnur Kuanyshkyzy Khassengaziyeva, Jan Urban, Dinara Bartunek, Sayat Ermukhanbetovich Sharakhmetov, Nazym Sapargaliyeva, Zhansulu Urgenishbayeva, Gulnar Bolatovna Kegenova, Eleonora Kozhabaeva, Mirgaliy Baimukanov, Boris Levin
pmc-11504185.description: Simple SummaryThe current state of rainbow trout, Oncorhynchus mykiss, was investigated 50 years after the first introduction of the species to the water bodies of the Balkhash basin. The wild form of the species from Kamchatka and the cultured form from European fish farms have successfully adapted to the local environmental conditions.

pmc-11592559.creator: Marcin Makowski, Edward W. Piotrowski
pmc-11592559.description: The concept of risk is fundamental in various scientific fields, including physics, biology and engineering, and is crucial for the study of complex systems, especially financial markets. pmc-12631402.title: Role of heparin-induced HGF release in the acute phase of STEMI
pmc-12631402.creator: S. Leboube, A. Paccalet, C. Brun, F. Moulin, B. Pillot, G. Bidaux, L. Mechtouff, H. Thibault, T. Bochaton, C. Crola Da Silva
pmc-12631402.description: IntroductionReperfusion injury remains a major limitation in the management of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Despite numerous preclinical successes, cardioprotective strategies have largely failed in clinical translation. Heparin, routinely administered for STEMI, may exert protective effects beyond anticoagulation through a rapid release of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), a known cardioprotective agent.

pmc-13102765.title: Hearing loss and incident dementia over 8 years in Black and White older adults: the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study
pmc-13102765.creator: Jennifer A. Deal, John J. Shin, Kening Jiang, A. Richey Sharrett, Josef Coresh, Rebecca F. Gottesman, David S. Knopman, Thomas Mosley, Keenan A. Walker, Frank R. Lin, Nicholas S. Reed
pmc-13102765.description: ObjectiveWe investigated potential racial disparities in the effects of audiometric hearing loss and its treatment on dementia and mortality among 3,602 older adults aged 68–89 years, 22% of whom were self-identified Black race.MethodsAdjudicated all-cause dementia was determined using neurocognitive test data, proxy reports, and surveillance of hospital records and death certificates.

pmc-13175518.title: Enhancing the Antibacterial and Biointegrative Properties of Microporous Titanium Surfaces Using Various Metal Coatings: A Comparative Study
pmc-13175518.creator: Maxim Shevtsov, Ekaterina Bozhokina, Natalia Yudintceva, Danila Bobkov, Anastasiya Lukacheva, Denis Nazarov, Irina Voronkina, Larisa Smagina, Emil Pitkin, Elena Oganesyan, Airat Kayumov, Grigory Raykhtsaum, Mykhailo Matviychuk, Vladimir Moxson, Michael Akkaoui, Stephanie E Combs, Mark Pitkin
